package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions of the malicious lookalike packages)
package_info.why_malicious: A large number of malicious packages were submitted to PyPI with names intentionally similar to established dependencies (typosquatting), aiming to deceive users into installing them. These packages execute code that exfiltrates sensitive data at install or import time, compromising the software supply chain by distributing malware.

execution_context.file_location: setup.py or __init__.py of the malicious package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or install-time, the code reads the contents of /etc/passwd and sends them via an HTTP request to a hardcoded external domain, resulting in unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive system data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code automatically reads a sensitive system file and transmits its contents to an external server without user knowledge or consent, which is a clear data exfiltration technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or transmit sensitive files such as /etc/passwd during installation or import, nor do they make unsolicited network requests at these stages.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may implement crash reporting or telemetry, but these typically send non-sensitive diagnostic data and always require explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Presence of network requests to hardcoded, untrusted domains in setup.py or __init__.py
Direct access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd) during install or import
Minimal or obfuscated code that combines file reading and network transmission in a single line
Execution of code with side effects at install-time or import-time

attack_chain.action: User installs a package with a name similar to a popular dependency (typosquatting), believing it to be legitimate.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code embedded in the package is executed during installation or import.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, reading sensitive files such as /etc/passwd and sending the data to an external server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated sensitive data, compromising the user's system and potentially enabling further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests initiated by setup.py or __init__.py during package installation or import
Access to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/id_rsa) by package installation or import scripts
Packages with names that closely resemble popular dependencies (typosquatting), especially those recently registered
file_indicators: setup.py or __init__.py containing single-line or obfuscated code that combines file access and network transmission
Presence of hardcoded URLs or domains in installation or import scripts
Package names that differ from popular libraries by a single character or common typo
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not associated with legitimate package maintainers (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
Connections to newly registered or untrusted domains during package installation or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for network activity initiated by setup.py or __init__.py during package installation or import, especially outbound requests to untrusted or unknown domains. Scan package files for code that accesses sensitive files or makes network requests at install/import time. Flag and manually review packages with names similar to popular dependencies, particularly if they contain suspicious code patterns or network activity.
